stem: A 3-year bond has a face value of Rs 10,000 and a coupon rate of 10% per annum paid annually. The required rate of return is 12% per annum. The bond value formula is: V = C x [(1-(1+r)^-n)/r] + F x (1+r)^-n, where C = annual coupon, F = face value, r = required rate, n = years. Given that (1.12)^3 = 1.4049, what is the fair value of this bond?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Equates bond value with face value (Rs 10,000), not recognising that 12% required return > 10% coupon implies a discount.

Discounts only the face value (10000/1.4049 = 7118) and does not add the PV of coupons, giving Rs 7,118; or uses the single coupon undiscounted and face discounted: 1000 x 3 + 7118 = 10118, arriving at a wrong figure. A student who takes PV of only year-3 coupon gets 10000*1.10^3 /1.12^3 = 13310/1.4049=9474, off by the year 1 and 2 coupons. The specific value Rs 8,929 arises from using n=2 instead of n=3 in the annuity factor while correctly discounting the face over 3 years.

Uses the coupon rate (10%) as the discount rate instead of the required rate (12%), computing bond value at r=10%: V = 1000*[(1-1/1.33)/0.10] + 10000/1.33 = 1000*2.49 + 7519 = 9749 approximately Rs 9,712: a rate-selection error.

explanation_sections.punchline: A multi-year bond value is the PV of an annuity of coupons plus the PV of the face value, both discounted at the required (market) rate.
explanation_sections.approach: Formula: V = C x PVIFA(r,n) + F x PVF(r,n). Map: C=1000, F=10000, r=0.12, n=3. Compute discount factor = 1/1.4049 = 0.7118. PVIFA = 0.2882/0.12 = 2.4017. PV coupons = 2401.7. PV face = 7118. Sum = 9519.7.
explanation_sections.lesson: Always discount using the required (market) rate, not the coupon rate; the coupon rate only sets the coupon cash flow.
explanation_sections.timing: 100 seconds. Trap: using coupon rate as discount rate. Quick check: since required rate > coupon rate, bond must be below Rs 10,000.
